limitations: OS target-window metadata is sampled, not continuous. On-screen flags do not prove uncovered pixels, compositor callbacks, physical HDR or A/V synchronization.

The shell waits for a fresh observer window proof before timestamped native menu/button actions. Earlier untimestamped DOM setup remains outside that handshake; startup DOM visibility is not qualified.

Timestamped native menu/button requests require shell-consumed fresh window proof, independently matched to a retained validated observation and its publication. The separate strict prior-query-end-before-request gate remains; this proves sampled metadata and request ordering, not continuous physical visibility.

Intentional window resize, minimize, close, return and fullscreen transitions are allowed. No all-interval visibility claim is made; unchanged frozen native checks retain their own phase-specific window requirements.

RSS covers the observed runner process group, PPID descendants and retained known descendants; independently managed XPC services and GPU allocations are not attributable through this process-tree metric.
Competing-work detection covers named native/build programs, not arbitrary unrecognized model workloads. The run still requires serialized local GPU/model work.
Pins establish unchanged input files. The runner's --shared argument hashes a path; existing native linkage selects the loaded image. This observer does not claim loaded-image identity.
